entry.title: [UPDATED] MAL-2026-16214: Malicious code in discord-resolvers (npm)
entry.content:
Malicious code in discord-resolvers (npm)

Aliases: GHSA-whmq-ffxc-4jpc

Affected:

  • discord-resolvers

--- _-= Per source details. Do not edit below this line.=-_ ## Source: amazon-inspector (6aa01ed90340a9458c2906ec74fd9277bb7d0e4da48ef09487639aa6c45e6791) The package published as discord-resolvers is unrelated to Discord. On require, index.js invokes startBackupLoop() at top level, which recursively archives the /root directory on Linux (or the drive root, typically C:\, on Windows) into a ZIP and uploads it via the Telegram Bot API to a hardcoded chat controlled by the package author. The loop repeats every hour and all errors are silently swallowed. The exclude list (node_modules,.git,.cache, tmp) does not exclude credential-bearing paths such as ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, ~/.npmrc,.env files, browser profiles, or wallet stores, so SSH keys, cloud credentials, source code, and other secrets unde…

entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-22qr-rp27-j9wm: PenPot MCP REPL server binds to 0.0.0.0 with unauthenticated /execute endpoint — RCE
entry.content:
PenPot MCP REPL server binds to 0.0.0.0 with unauthenticated /execute endpoint — RCE

Aliases: CVE-2026-45805

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:A/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H

Affected:

  • @penpot/mcp — fixed in 2.15.0

### Summary The MCP module's `ReplServer` binds to all interfaces (`0.0.0.0:4403`) and exposes a `/execute` endpoint that runs arbitrary code with zero authentication. Anyone on the network can POST JavaScript and it runs on the server. entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-vx52-2968-3vc6: pnpm: Environment secrets exfiltrated via env-placeholder expansion in proxy settings read from an untrusted pnpm-workspace.yaml
entry.content:
pnpm: Environment secrets exfiltrated via env-placeholder expansion in proxy settings read from an untrusted pnpm-workspace.yaml

Aliases: CVE-2026-101043

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:N/A:N

Affected:

  • pnpm — fixed in 11.11.0
  • pnpm — fixed in 10.34.5

## Summary pnpm expands `${VAR}` environment placeholders in the `httpProxy` / `httpsProxy` / `noProxy` settings read from a project's `pnpm-workspace.yaml`. Because a project manifest is repository-controlled, a malicious repository that a victim merely clones and runs `pnpm install` in can route all install traffic through an attacker proxy whose hostname or userinfo embeds — and thereby exfiltrates — an environment secret such as `NPM_TOKEN` or `GITHUB_TOKEN`. This bypasses a trust boundary pnpm deliberately enforces: env-placeholder expansion of request-destination settings is already suppressed for `registry`, `pnprServer`, `registries` and `namedRegistries` when they come from an untrusted project manifest, and the sibling `.npmrc` reader already classifies the proxy keys as reques…

entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-9gfj-28hw-jchp: Knowns Unrestricted Path Traversal leading to out-of-bounds arbitrary .md file read, write, and deletion in MCP Docs + Memory Tools
entry.content:
Knowns Unrestricted Path Traversal leading to out-of-bounds arbitrary .md file read, write, and deletion in MCP Docs + Memory Tools

Aliases: CVE-2026-86439

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H

Affected:

  • knowns — fixed in 0.30.0

## Overview Verified. Multiple **Unrestricted Path Traversal** vulnerabilities exist in the Knowns MCP `docs` and `memory` tools, allowing arbitrary file read, write, and deletion operations outside the project sandbox. The storage layer functions (`Get`, `Create`, `Update`, `Rename`, `Delete`) in both `doc_store.go` and `memory_store.go` concatenate user-controlled paths with `filepath.Join()` without any containment validation. Additionally, the `docs.update` action with a `newPath` parameter performs a file deletion via `Rename()`, but is classified as `CapWrite` in the permission registry rather than `CapDelete`. This allows an attacker with a `read-write-no-delete` preset to bypass deletion restrictions and destroy arbitrary files outside the project root. ## Affected paths | Fil…

entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-29h2-jr22-frmh: OpenZeppelin Confidential Contracts `VestingWalletConfidential`: a malicious ERC-7984 token is able to extract private data from the vesting wallet
entry.content:
OpenZeppelin Confidential Contracts `VestingWalletConfidential`: a malicious ERC-7984 token is able to extract private data from the vesting wallet

Severity: CVSS_V4: CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:L/UI:N/VC:H/VI:N/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N

Affected:

  • @openzeppelin/confidential-contracts — fixed in 0.3.2
  • @openzeppelin/confidential-contracts — fixed in 0.4.2
  • @openzeppelin/confidential-contracts — fixed in 0.5.2

### Impact Two locations consume an encrypted handle returned by an untrusted external party and use it without verifying that the party is ACL-authorized on it. #### `VestingWalletConfidential` Malicious users can call `release` with a malicious token. This token could return an alternative handle on `confidentialBalanceOf`, which represents the balance of the vesting wallet on an alternative ERC-7984 token (or any other handle that the vesting wallet has access to). The vesting wallet does not check that the token has ACL access and grants access to a new handle derived from the returned handle. Effectively, this bug allows a malicious user to gain information about any private `euint64` handle that the vesting wallet has access to via a malicious ERC-7984 token. There is no loss of …
